chunks: And with the foregoing chain of narration from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Hamza ibn Humran who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:

Whenever any one of you is determined to do good, then he should not delay it. For it may be that a servant offers a prayer or fasts a day, and then it is said to him: Do whatever you wish after this, for Allah has forgiven you.

key_terms.غفر: Ghafara: to forgive, to cover over sins; divine forgiveness (maghfira) is a central Quranic and hadith theme
key_terms.همّ: Hamma: to resolve, to be determined to do something; indicates firm intention preceding action

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about not delaying good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports a saying emphasizing the urgency of doing good deeds without delay. The hadith teaches that when a believer resolves to do something good, they should act immediately rather than postpone it. The rationale given is remarkable: a servant of God may offer a single prayer or fast a single day, and that act alone could earn divine forgiveness for all their subsequent deeds. This reflects the Shia understanding that sincerity and promptness in worship can bring immeasurable divine grace, and that procrastination in good deeds risks losing an opportunity that may never return.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 37. And with the foregoing chains of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from ‘Ali ibn Hadeed, from ‘Ali ibn al-Nu’man, from Hamzah ibn Hamran who said: I heard Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, say: "

Whenever anyone of you is determined to do good, then he should not delay doing it. For it might so be that a slave of Allah offered prayers or kept a day’s fast and then he is told: Do whatever you desire after this, for I have forgiven you."
